summary.title: How to Do Code Reviews Like a Human (Part One)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to run code reviews that treat the review as a social process as well as a technical one, using automation, style guides, fast turnaround, gentle phrasing, and principle-based notes.
keywords: linters and formatters in code review
avoid saying you in code review
takeaways: Automate mechanical checks like builds, tests, formatting, and linting so reviewers can focus on functional errors and readability.
Settle style debates with a style guide, adopted, built incrementally, or a hybrid of both.
Start reviews quickly, with a maximum turnaround of about one business day, and keep changelists small.
Phrase feedback to avoid accusatory wording: avoid 'you', frame notes as requests, and ground them in principles with objective language.
Review high-level design issues first and keep notes and code examples limited per round to avoid overwhelming the author.
summary.summary: The article argues that code review advice often focuses only on finding bugs and ignores how feedback lands on the author. It defines a code review as a formal, written, multi-round process ending in LGTM, and explains why it is hard: written criticism can read as a personal attack. The author then gives eight techniques, each with concrete examples such as a before-and-after table for automated formatting, a list of CI and linter tools, and rewritten comments that avoid the word "you". The piece is conversational and example-driven rather than a formal tutorial.
